celaleyn:1-1.t: This sūra and the one after it were revealed when Labīd the Jew bewitched the Prophet ﷺ by means of a bowstring with eleven knots in it. Allah informed him of that and of its location, so it was brought before him ﷺ, and he was commanded to seek refuge with the two sūras. Whenever he recited a verse of them a knot came undone and he felt lighter, until all the knots came undone and he rose as though released from a hobble. ﴿قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ الْفَلَقِ﴾: the daybreak,

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ﴾, of living beings, accountable and non-accountable, and inanimate things such as poison and other things,

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿وَمِنْ شَرِّ غَاسِقٍ إِذَا وَقَبَ﴾, that is, the night when it grows dark, or the moon when it disappears,

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿وَمِنْ شَرِّ النَّفَّاثَاتِ﴾: the sorceresses who blow ﴿فِي الْعُقَدِ﴾ that they tie in the thread, blowing on them with something they say, without spittle; al-Zamakhsharī said: with it — such as the daughters of the aforementioned Labīd,

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿وَمِنْ شَرِّ حَاسِدٍ إِذَا حَسَدَ﴾, that is, shows his envy and acts according to what it requires, like the aforementioned Labīd, of the Jews who envied the Prophet ﷺ. The mention of the three, which «ما خلق» already includes, after it, is because of the intensity of their evil.
